Welcome to Unified Academy
We are a special school for boys aged 9 to 16 who have social, emotional and mental health needs, and all of our students have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP). At Unified Academy, students are at the centre of every decision we make. Our aim is to support each young person to become a confident, respectful and well‑rounded adult with high aspirations for their future.
We offer a highly personalised approach to education, carefully tailored to meet the individual needs, abilities and interests of our students. Class sizes are small, with no more than ten students per teaching group, enabling staff to deliver purposeful, engaging and well‑structured learning. Alongside teaching staff, classroom assistants provide additional support, helping students to build confidence and self‑esteem while developing academically, socially and emotionally.
Our students have access to a range of therapeutic support, including Trusted Adults, Emotional Literacy Support Assistants (ELSAs) and Canine Assisted Learning (CAL). We also have full‑time Home School Link Workers (HSLWs), who work closely with families to support behaviour, attendance and access to wider Health and Social Care services.
At Unified Academy, we nurture and encourage every student to make the most of their school experience. We value and celebrate their individuality, strengths and achievements.
We are fully committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all children and young people. Safeguarding is at the heart of our culture, and we work tirelessly to ensure that every student feels safe, respected and supported. All staff receive regular safeguarding training, and we work in close partnership with families and external agencies to maintain the highest standards of care and protection.
If you are considering a place at Unified Academy for your son, please get in touch with us at info@unifiedacademy.org or call 01737 215 488.
Annabelle Thomas – Principal

Testimonials
The staff at this school have been amazing with my son from year 7 all the way to year 11. Understanding, sensitive and flexible to his needs. They have gone over and above to make sure he accesses education and continues to grow emotionally and socially. I couldn’t be prouder of the man he’s becoming - Thank you.
Words cannot express how grateful I am to you and all the support you have given my son (and me). He came to you a shell of a boy, with very little confidence not knowing who he was and he felt he was not capable of much at all. He is now leaving more confident, happy and able to discuss his difficulties openly and going to college. I have my boy/young man back. Thank you so very much.

Personal Development
Personal Development sessions are offered to all students in years 7 -11 with varied on and off-site activities that focus on developing key social, creative, digital, physical, cultural and cognitive skills and awareness in order to build independence, resilience and character. Personal Development sessions aim to enhance the curriculum offer and extend beyond the academic through offering broad and varied activities that allow students to engage positively with the wider community, experiencing a sense of belonging and supporting students to become responsible and active citizens. Sessions promote students spiritual, moral, social and cultural development as well as building on student’s awareness of fundamental British values such as democracy, individual liberty, rule of law, respect and tolerance. Opportunities for students to be reflective, to learn, to behave with integrity and to cooperate consistently with others are imbedded within all sessions. Students are able to sign up for Personal Development sessions for 6 week periods, gaining an AQA Unit Award Certificate at the end of the course. Topic (KS3 Humanities)
At Unified Academy, history education will help students to gain a working knowledge and understanding of Britain’s past and that of the wider world. It will inspire students’ curiosity to know more about the past. Teaching will equip students to ask perceptive questions, think critically, analyse evidence, evaluate arguments and develop perspective and judgement. Their studies in this subject will help them to evaluate the impact that historical events have had on their lives and society today. They will learn how democracy has developed and grown over the centuries. History helps students to understand the complexity of people’s lives, the processes of and reasons for change over time, the diversity of societies, the relationships between different groups and the challenges humans have faced at different times
At Unified Academy Geography inspires our students to have a curiosity and fascination about the world and its people that will remain with them for the rest of their lives. Students will compare geographical locations; investigating trade, environmental impact, climate, natural hazards, population, culture, erosion and how the UK fits in the 21st century world. Students will be more confident discussing their community, heritage and culture as they progress into adulthood.
Students will complete end-of-topic assessments, present completed work and receive accreditation to recognise their learning by completing AQA Unit Awards.

Maths
Our ambitious mathematics curriculum not only seeks to provide our students with the skills that they need for school, but also to enhance their life skills and to prepare them for the next stage of their education, training or work. We seek to challenge and extend all our students, including the most able, to achieve worthwhile accreditation to support their futures.
Our programme of work is planned to build on the stepping stones within each area of study. Students can access our curriculum at the best stage for them rather than on an age basis. They revisit the topics regularly and build on earlier learning so that by the end of Yr11, they understand and apply the ideas and skills to the best of their ability. A range of pathways allows our students to access mathematical knowledge at the levels most suited to their needs. Regular and varied assessments ensure that students achieve as well as they can for their given stage.
Our staff concentrate not only on knowledge and skills but also on finding the best approaches for teaching mathematics to our students. The use of problem-solving projects related to real life activities helps our students to engage with mathematics. We aim to develop our students’ creativity, resourcefulness and resilience through their day-to-day mathematical activities.
In Year 11, students will have the opportunity to gain either a Functional Skills or GCSE qualification in mathematics.

PSHE (inc. RE)
Personal, social, health and economic education (PSHE) is an essential part of all students’ education. At Unified Academy, the PSHE curriculum enables all students develop the knowledge, skills and attributes they need to keep themselves healthy, safe, and prepared for life. Our PSHE programme and the universal PHSE offer aims to have an impact on both student’s academic and social outcomes. PSHE education contributes to our school’s statutory duties including the Equality Act (2010) to provide a balanced and broadly-based curriculum. Our PSHE offer addresses; substance misuse and its dangers, healthy eating, the importance of physical and mental health citizenship, British values, budgeting and other key skills for life. These are addressed through the core themes of ‘Health and Wellbeing’, ‘Living in the Wider World’ and ‘Relationships’. Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) is embedded within our PSHE framework. PSHE at Unified Academy will address barriers to learning, raise aspirations, and improve the life chances of all students.
Religious Education (RE)
At Unified Academy Religious Education (RE) is delivered through our PSHE lessons and tutorial sessions. Religion and beliefs shape our values and our behaviour. RE develops students’ knowledge and understanding of the faiths that form part of contemporary society. It encourages young people to ask challenging questions about the meaning and purpose of life and issues of right and wrong. RE develops students’ knowledge and understanding of the principal world faiths and also contributes to students’ personal development and well-being. Students should understand and respect the range of different cultures and spirituality within the school and further afield as an essential element of their preparation for adult life in the modern world and a diverse society.
If parents/carers wish to withdraw their child from all or part of RE please contact Nicola Ebdon nebdon@unifiedacademy.org
Students in Year 10 and 11 will work towards gaining BTEC Level 1 or 2 qualification in Personal Growth and Wellbeing.

Art and Photography
Art is a subject that can help us to understand and give meaning to the world in which we live. We develop students’ awareness of the impact of art on society and how artist/practitioners work is constantly re-used in the visual arts such as fine art, TV, media, graphics, film, music video and movies.
Through our Art & Design curriculum we seek to engage, inspire and challenge students, equipping them with skills to experiment, invent, improve and create their own original pieces of work. Over time they will develop their ability to think critically as well as increase their knowledge and understanding of Art & Design. To self-express, to gain a sense of fulfilment and to enjoy.
The curriculum explores many practical skills in handling the variety of specialised equipment and materials/ media. Motor skills are continually refined and work adjusted to improve the visual impact, structure and composition, for example. These skills are transferable to careers in design, painting and decorating, media/film/theatre etc. technology technicians etc.
Each term, core skills, the formal elements and the Subject Thresholds are revisited in a spiral learning format to embed and extend understanding and engagement. Written responses use writing frames and invite opinion and connections.
During KS4, students prepare a portfolio of work based on responses to art skills, approaches and concepts, and then extend this to their own interests.
Learners develop oracy, creative thinking, visual literacy and develop highly valuable and transferrable skills for future careers and life. Our themes link with selected artist/ practitioner works including traditional, modern and contemporary ideas, concepts and knowledge
In KS4 students work towards GCSE in Art and Design or AQA Unit Awards.

English
In our English programme at Unified Academy, we aim to teach students to speak and write fluently so that they can communicate information and ideas clearly to others. We seek to enable students to express themselves confidently and accurately in a broad range of situations. We focus on all four areas of language: speaking, listening, reading and writing. Through their reading and listening, students will increase their knowledge and will develop their ability to understand and respect the views of others. English and literacy are key elements of learning; they enable students to understand and interact with every kind of written text. At Unified Academy, we value reading as a key life skill and have developed three pathways to support all students to learn to read. Currently we use the following reading schemes, Phonological Awareness Training (PAT), That Reading Thing, and Accelerated Reader. We aim to ensure that students leave us with the ability to read fluently, with comprehension and to build a lifelong love of reading.
At Unified Academy English and Literacy is embedded through teaching and learning practice. We believe that a strong foundation of English and Literacy leads to success, both at school and in adult life. Unified Academy is committed to raising standards of English and Literacy in order to raise standards and attainment across the curriculum. All students leave Unified Academy ready to meaningfully engage in their local community and be equipped to shape and transform the world they live in. Throughout their time with us, students will achieve a range of formal qualifications in English, ranging from Entry Level Certificates and Functional Skills qualifications to GCSE English Language.

Science
Science education provides the foundations for understanding the world through its component areas of biology, chemistry and physics. Students will learn how science can change and improve our lives and is vital to national prosperity.
Our science curriculum is planned to evoke curiosity, enquiry and understanding about the world around our students through a scientific eye. The curriculum allows students to develop key skills that prepare learners for adulthood and the world of work. Providing the skills to challenge and ask questions through the development of both knowledge and skill across the breadth of science disciplines. The curriculum provides regular opportunities for practical work and offering opportunities for children to learn outdoors where appropriate.
At the end of Year 11, students have the opportunity to gain national qualification in science, either Entry Level or GCSEs.

Alternative Learning Provision (ALP)
At Unified Academy, alternative learning provision (ALP) is arranged to ensure that all students who for any reason cannot access the in-school provision are given purposeful and appropriate programmes of learning. The ALP offer is arranged using a range of providers who are experienced and suitably qualified to provide alternative learning for our students.
Our ALP is planned to ensure that it meets the specific needs of students and enables them to re-engage with learning in an alternative setting. All students receive a sound education, regardless of their circumstances or the settings in which they find themselves. Provision will differ from student to student. Food and Nutrition
At Unified Academy, Food and Nutrition enables students to develop awareness of the made and natural environment and the social contexts into which food technology plays an important role. Food Technology aims to foster curiosity, ingenuity and imagination through personal involvement with nutritional concepts and ingredients. It also strives to increase students’ understanding of the physical, social, emotional, cultural needs of the individual, which changes throughout the stages of their life.
Students have opportunities to plan, prepare and create products that fulfil a wide variety of culinary requirements that meet the needs of individual students. In the Food and Nutrition learning environment staff insist upon high standards of health and safety, personal hygiene, food hygiene practices and following clear instructions to create as near as possible a working kitchen. The students respect rules associated with “the trade” and recognise that their behaviours need to be professional and acknowledging of boundaries. Within the environment all students and staff work well together as a team to achieve positive outcomes.
At KS4, students work towards a BTEC Level 1 Award in Home Cooking Skills as well as studying for GCSE in Food Preparation and Nutrition.
Food Technology Learning Journey

Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
At Unified Academy, ICT education equips students with skills and knowledge that are essential for future success in the working world, as well as important elements in their leisure and social lives. ICT has links with mathematics, science and design and technology. Students will be taught how to communicate safely online by developing clear and robust internet protocols. Learning in ICT also ensures that students become digitally literate and are able to express themselves and develop their ideas through technology in ways that meet the needs of the future workplace and of active participants in a digital world.
Students are equipped to use ICT to create programs, systems and a range of content. They will learn about the various applications of computers, for example in writing, publishing, using email, accessing websites, constructing spreadsheets and using the internet for individual research. They will be able to articulate the impact that their skills and knowledge in ICT can have on their futures.
KS4 students will gather evidence to support achieving the OCR Level 1 iMedia Award, or the Level 1 Award in Essential Digital Skills for Work & Life

Careers Guidance
During their time at Unified Academy, students learn through an enriched curriculum which develops the skills and attitudes required to enable students to become successful and independent within adulthood. Students are guided throughout their curriculum with personalised targets to ensure that each learning experience is meaningful and helps every individual achieve their full potential.
Unified Academy supports careers development through high quality and personalised work experience opportunities, internal enterprise projects as well as bespoke planning and preparation of student career pathways.
We are committed to working in partnership with the local community and surrounding areas. If you are an employer or company that think you could help inspire our students within their career decisions, please contact Jeremy Crouch jcrouch@unifiedacademy.org or by telephone on 01737 215488.
Through every stage at Unified Academy, learning is focussed on developing student’s future pathways. Our Careers Programme lists some of the elements of careers information, advice and guidance that a student will encounter during their time with us.
